notes: Rules for Yerba Buena Island's L1 context scenery (tools/lib/ybi-context-generation.mjs): its terrain, ground cover, buildings, at-grade roads and paths, and procedural vegetation. YBI stays non-playable and non-colliding. Distances are metres, world x east and z south.

Evidence: the frozen OSM snapshot (2026-08-27); the 2026-05-26 Vantor aerial's cover classes (data/ybi/ybi-land-cover-2026-05-26.json); J. Clark, Birds and Wildlife of Yerba Buena Island, Initial Findings March-June 2017 and the 2016 initial findings (SF/TIDA): 'Blue Gum Eucalyptus is the most abundant tree species' on the north and northeast slopes above Clipper Cove, with Monterey cypress and acacia toward their top and middle, coast live oak and toyon at the top and middle and arroyo willow in the lower portions; the summit and the north- and east-facing slopes above Macalla Road hold 'the biggest stand of pines' (Monterey pine) among blue gum and acacia; the west coastal bluffs 'low-growing, wind-sculpted Coast-live Oaks' with coastal scrub. Dated views from Treasure Island: Street View Sep 2025 (17 Treasure Island Rd, headings 145-150), Mar 2025 (causeway), Nov 2025 (1 Clipper Cove Way, Avenue N), and the Commons photo 'Yerba Buena Island Profile - May 2025 01' (9yz, 2025-05-27).

Every value here is production inference from that evidence, not survey data. Plants are never listed by position: trees stand where the aerial's canopy reads, thinned by noise, and their species, size and spacing follow these rules.

buildings.evidence: OSM height, then building:levels at storey_m plus a parapet; otherwise a height by type. Apartments and residential: four storeys, from Street View Nov 2025 at 299 Macalla Rd (the Cove townhouse row, three floors and a roof deck over a ground floor) and Sep 2025 at 36 Meadow Drive (four floors). Houses two storeys. Storage tanks: the three round water tanks by the summit (2026-05-26 aerial), height inferred. Flat roofs unless roofs lists a form seen in a dated photo.

Torpedo Assembly Building (Building 262): a stone gable end in a Google Maps contributor photo, Nov 2022.

tree_clearance.evidence: Round the sculpture the crest stays low: from Treasure Island's west shore one low round crown stands left of it (the trees by the steps south-east of the plaza) and the plaza's parapet right of it, nothing reaching the steel ('Yerba Buena Island Profile - May 2025 01', 9yz, 2025-05-27); the close photo of the same day shows none taller than the cone, and the 2026-05-26 aerial shows only low shrubs and small trees within 80 m (the summit park and the crest north of its road loop). So within 80 m a crown keeps its top under the sculpture's foot on the side towards Treasure Island (a crown nearer Treasure Island shows higher against it from there) and under the cone's 6 m on the far side, and a species too tall for that stands as a low coast live oak (production inference).

evidence: Form: the plaque at the sculpture (owner photo, 2026-11-07): 'Point of Infinity. Surface of Revolution with Constant Negative Curvature', x = cos u / cosh v, y = sin u / cosh v, z = v - tanh v (0 <= u < 2 pi, 0 <= v < infinity): a pseudosphere, radius 1 at its rim (v = 0, z = 0), narrowing to a point as z rises.

Height 21.03 m (69 ft): KQED, A. Proehl, 'A New Piece of Public Art Makes a Point Above Yerba Buena Island', 2023-06-09 (updated 2024-01-11); Secret San Francisco, J. Ferrell, 2023-04-12; Wikipedia 'Point of Infinity' (checked 2026-11-07). OSM w1232537986 height=21.

Base radius 3.5 m: a 23 ft (7.01 m) base (KQED; Secret San Francisco: 23 feet across), OSM width=7 and its mapped 7 m circle. v_max then follows from R (v_max - tanh v_max) = 21.03 m: v_max = 7.009, a tip 12.7 mm across (Secret San Francisco gives 21 mm; the sources round).

Materials: a base of 8 glass-fibre-reinforced concrete panels and above it mirror-polished marine-grade stainless steel to the tip (KQED; Secret San Francisco). The spire shader (game/resources/materials/world/ybi/ybi_spire.gdshader) starts the steel 6.0 m up, where the pseudosphere is 0.9 m across: inferred from the close photo 'Point of Infinity Sculpture with SF and Bay Bridge, May 2025' (9yz, 2025-05-27), whose steel starts about 0.13 of the base's width across, and consistent with 'Yerba Buena Island Profile - May 2025 01' (9yz, 2025-05-27), where the concrete cone shows a few metres above the plaza's wall.

Place: OSM w1232537986's circle (centroid lon -122.3689838, lat 37.8104748; world x 176.41, z 1479.07), on the plaza over the decommissioned water tank in Hilltop Park (Secret San Francisco; KQED). The 2026-05-26 aerial shows the base's white disc about 10 m east and 1 m north of that centroid (about 7 m once the imagery's 2-4 m offset round the plaza is allowed for); Wikipedia's 37.81056 N, 122.36889 W (rounded to 1 arc second, about 30 m) lies 8 m east and 10 m north. The OSM position is kept. Base height: the USGS 2023 bare-earth DEM reads 97.02 m at the centroid, on the plaza's flat top (97.0-97.6 m across 40 m), 7.7 m below the island's summit (104.76 m) 280 m to the east.

bed.evidence: The cone stands in a round bed of white gravel inside a light concrete curb (close photo 'Point of Infinity Sculpture with SF and Bay Bridge, May 2025', 9yz, 2025-05-27; the 2026-05-26 aerial's pale disc round the base, about 9-10 m across). The bed's width, about 1.5 times the cone's, the curb's width and height are production inference from those two.

surfaces.seam_ramp_evidence: Owner request 2026-11-08: a thin light line showed across both carriageways at the causeway seam. Treasure Island's road skin lies 0.078 m over its land (its paths 0.08 m) and YBI's surfaces 0.1 m over its terrain, which meets the land edge to edge at the seam, so the 22 mm step showed the ground through it. The playable roads' and paths' runs past the outline now leave the seam at Treasure Island's own height for their class and rise to bias_m over seam_ramp_m, and their paint with them.
surfaces.evidence: Widths follow the Treasure Island road classes (tools/lib/world-contract.mjs ROAD_WIDTHS_M); steps as footways, links and construction roads as their aerial width. The on-grade Treasure Island Road works on the west shore (highway=construction, construction=tertiary) are drawn as the graded gravel the 2026-05-26 aerial shows. A construction way that names no road class (highway=construction alone) is a 4 m graded track (unspecified_construction_width_m), as the aerial shows the west-side haul roads.

grade_points.name: eastbound I-80 at grade, east end (about 51-52 m)

bridge_track.evidence: The Bay Bridge track owns I-80, its ramps and bridge- or tunnel-tagged ways (research 2026-11-07, section 1.3; interface points from the bridge owner, 2026-11-07, east/north metres with DEM heights). On-grade I-80 and ramps (a road cut from the east portal to about (634, -1386) at 51-52 m), the ramps' grade points and the tunnel portals are kept clear of YBI trees and buildings and drawn as a bare cut. Under the elevated structures (bridge-tagged ways and the man_made=bridge areas, including the transition decks over the senior officers' quarters gardens at about 51-59 m) trees may stand, but their tops stay below deck_clear_top_m; the bridge owner adds the columns.

far_scrub.evidence: Beyond near_limit_m the scrub stands as sparser, larger clumps: the coyote brush and toyon mounds, 1-3 m high and 2-4 m across, that break up the west face and the slopes below the crest in the 2025-05-27 photo and the 2026-05-26 aerial.

blue_gum.evidence: Blue gum (Eucalyptus globulus): tall, ragged, airy crowns, the tallest in the deep groves of the lower north slope and the south-east wood (Commons 2025-05-27, Street View Sep and Nov 2025, where the canopy stays below the crest's new buildings): the kit's mature eucalyptus (22-25 m) at about 21-32 m, smaller at a grove's edge.

acacia.evidence: Black acacia stands in as the kit's dense dark broad dome; its species is not modelled on its own.

willow.evidence: Arroyo willow along the cove's lower slope and beach, as a low rounded broadleaf.

garden_tree.evidence: OSM natural=tree nodes round the Senior Officers' Quarters gardens and the Coast Guard station; species not recorded.

scrub.evidence: Coastal scrub, coyote brush and French broom (Clark 2017; CNPS Yerba Buena chapter) as the kit's mounded shrubs.

vegetation.zones_evidence: Clark 2017 by zone: on the Clipper Cove woodland blue gum is the most abundant tree, with Monterey cypress and acacia toward the slope's top and middle, coast live oak and toyon at its top and middle and arroyo willow low down (cove_upper and cove_lower split the slope at 35 m); the summit holds the island's biggest stand of Monterey pine; the west bluffs low, wind-sculpted coast live oaks with coastal scrub. The west bluffs' tall stands, the band between the west-side road works and Yerba Buena Road's summit loop, are blue gum (the 2025-05-27 photo from Treasure Island's west shore; the 2026-05-26 aerial's crowns and long shadows); the wind-sculpted oaks stand in their scrub as small trees.
vegetation.upper_slope_evidence: Above 45 m (the slopes below the crest, cleared and replanted round the new housing and roads 2016-2022) trees stand lower: the canopy reads below the crest's buildings from Treasure Island (Street View Sep 2025 sv02, Mar 2025 sv03, Nov 2025 sv04).
vegetation.tallness_evidence: The 2026-05-26 aerial's deep shadow (data/ybi shadow layer) separates the island's tall groves from its low scrub: in the north cove woodland, the south and south-east slopes and the trees along the bridge 17-40 % of the canopy's surroundings lie in deep shadow, in the scrub of the west face, the summit park and the knob 2-10 % (round 2 debug, notes/shadow-debug.png). The Commons photo of 2025-05-27 and Street View Sep 2025 (sv02) show the same split: tall groves on the cove shore band and the south-east, open gold grass and low dark scrub on the west face and summit. The shadow counts in and round the canopy within 10 m, since a narrow band of tall trees throws its shadow onto the open ground beside it (the west-side band, which the canopy-only count took for scrub in round 2); shadow within structure_shadow_m of a building or the bridge is left out. Where the stand reads tallest (tall_band), its rim trees keep their full height: the west-side band of blue gums stands 25-35 m high along its whole width in the 2025-05-27 photo. The shadow of a wall or of the summit reservoir's banks is left out like a building's, and the share is taken over at least min_canopy_share of the window, so a speck of crowns beside a dark wall or bank does not read as a tall stand (round 4: two crest blue gums by the summit plaza stood as high as the sculpture's tip from Treasure Island). The tallest stands (tall_band) also open no clearings: the west-side blue-gum band stands as a near-solid mass up to the bridge tower in the 2025-05-27 photo.

understorey.evidence: Under and between the blue gums: acacia, young oak, toyon and blackberry scrub (Clark 2017), which hides the trunks from Treasure Island except where a grove stands open.

vegetation.tints_evidence: The impostors' tone at a distance, YBI's own (Treasure Island's trees keep theirs): darker and warmer than the shared tint so the groves read as the dark olive masses of the 2025-05-27 photo (about sRGB 49,50,35 in its groves) through the game's haze, the blue gums a little greyer and lighter than the cypress and pine.
vegetation.zones_note: Zones apply in order, the first whose rule holds: when lists alternatives (any may hold), each a set of conditions that must all hold (in_osm_wood, elevation_above_m, elevation_below_m, x_below, z_below, normal_x_below, normal_z_below, shore_within_m; world x, z with z = -north, the terrain's unit normal); an empty list always holds.

ground.evidence: Channels (red forest floor and dark scrub, green herbaceous green, blue bare soil, sand and graded fill, alpha rock) over the default dry straw, from the aerial's cover classes, the canopy and scrub rules above, OSM natural=scrub, bare_rock, cliff and beach, landuse=grass and leisure=garden areas, the shore and the slope.

facades_note: Only buildings with a dated photo carry a façade's coarse banding (window and floor bands, bays); every other YBI building stays neutral L1 with no invented detail.

walls.evidence: OSM barrier=retaining_wall and barrier=wall ways on YBI's land. A retaining wall's height is the 2023 DEM's step across it (3 m either side) plus a coping, as the pale walls along Macalla Road (Street View Sep 2025 sv02, Mar 2025 sv03) and the board-formed wall under The Bristol (ybi02, Nov 2025) stand; a freestanding wall 1.2 m (production inference).

causeway_paint.evidence: Owner request 2026-11-08: the road markings broke off at the seam between Treasure Island and the YBI causeway road. Treasure Island Road leaves the island as two one-way carriageways (OSM w1115934722, lanes=2, and w1249797943, lanes=1) round a raised concrete median and continues up YBI as w1115934722 and w513879523. Each carriageway takes a white edge line on its right and a yellow line on its median side, and where the carriageways meet the yellow lines close into a double yellow, to the hilltop junction with Macalla Road; paint stops junction_clear_m off every road that crosses or joins. Line width, double-line gap, edge inset and paint lift are Treasure Island's own (tools/config/street-detail-zones.json street_ground lines and lifts), paint wear the new district's (tools/config/street-ground.json). Production inference read with the 2026-05-26 aerial (Esri Wayback 43291, z19), which shows edge lines along both carriageways and the median running on onto YBI.

basin.evidence: The summit reservoir (OSM w1249412146, natural=water, water=basin) is concrete-lined: the 2026-05-26 aerial shows its green water inside pale banks. From Treasure Island's west shore its south-east bank is the 'large exposed cut' below the summit in 'Yerba Buena Island Profile - May 2025 01' (9yz, 2025-05-27): a flat-topped, steep face of weathered dark grey concrete over a pale tan band (the USGS 2023 DEM falls from 89 m on that side to the 71 m water). The water lies on the level ground of the mapped area (rising at most 0.15 m a metre); the banks, in the walls' weathered concrete, are the rest of that area and the ground within 14 m outside it that rises at least 0.6 m a metre (about 31 degrees); the gentler ground round them keeps its cover (production inference).
